plates.side_label: JUNE–AUGUST 1937 KREBS & JOHNSON (ENZYMOLOGIA 4: 148–156): 8-STEP CITRIC ACID CYCLE (OXALOACETATE + ACETYL-COA → CITRATE → 2 CO2 + 3 NADH + 1 FADH2 + 1 GTP)

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked 8-step Krebs Citric Acid Cycle diagram from Krebs & Johnson (August 1937, Enzymologia 4: 148–156) shows 2-carbon acetyl-CoA condensing with 4-carbon oxaloacetate to form 6-carbon citrate, then stepping through isocitrate, alpha-ketoglutarate, succinyl-CoA, succinate, fumarate, and malate to release 2 CO2 molecules and load 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, and 1 GTP/ATP per turn.

teach_overlay.label: 1937 KREBS CYCLE: 4-C OXALOACETATE + 2-C ACETYL-COA → 6-C CITRATE → 2 CO2 EXHALED + 3 NADH + 1 FADH2 + 1 GTP
teach_overlay.detail: Inked 8-step Krebs Citric Acid Cycle diagram on period paper from Krebs & Johnson (August 1937, Enzymologia 4: 148–156) showing 2-carbon acetyl-CoA condensing with 4-carbon oxaloacetate to form 6-carbon citrate, then stepping through isocitrate, alpha-ketoglutarate, succinyl-CoA, succinate, fumarate, and malate to release 2 CO2 molecules and load 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, and 1 GTP/ATP per turn
teach_overlay.scale: the Krebs cycle works like a waterwheel that never gets used up — a four-carbon bucket picks up a two-carbon piece of food, drops off two carbon dioxide molecules that you breathe out of your lungs, and comes right back around for the next load
